projects.name: Personal Portfolio — Hand-Coded Cinematic Site
projects.core_idea: Hand-coded personal portfolio site with cinematic animations and a custom six-layer cursor — no frameworks, no build step.
projects.problem: Template-built portfolio sites all look the same and hide whether the author can actually write frontend code; this one proves it with pure hand-written HTML, CSS and JavaScript.
projects.features: Custom six-layer cursor | GSAP 3 + ScrollTrigger scroll animations | Lenis inertia smooth-scroll | aurora video backgrounds | split-text reveals | 3D card tilt | fully responsive
projects.what: Hand-coded personal portfolio site with cinematic animations and a custom six-layer cursor — no frameworks, no build step. A live personal portfolio site with cinematic motion design, served straight from GitHub Pages with zero build tooling.
projects.how: Vanilla JavaScript modules drive GSAP 3 timelines and ScrollTrigger scenes; Lenis handles inertia scrolling and Splitting.js powers per-character text reveals; deployed on GitHub Pages with no bundler.
projects.outcome: Live on GitHub Pages; fully responsive and framework-free, demonstrating raw HTML/CSS/JS and animation engineering.

projects.name: Gnosis — AI Agent Automation Platform
projects.core_idea: A production-minded AI agent platform that turns natural-language automation descriptions into deployable agents, with 4-tier memory, self-learning loops, RPA and multi-agent swarms.
projects.problem: Non-technical teams cannot build or operate AI agents; Gnosis packages agent creation, memory, learning, execution and monitoring behind one dashboard and one API, without managing LLM providers or infrastructure.
projects.features: Agent Factory (natural language to deployment plan) | 4-tier memory (correction, episodic, procedural, semantic) with FAISS retrieval | 3-loop self-learning: instant corrections, pattern extraction, periodic evolution | Dream + Oracle engines for idle-time simulation and cross-agent insights | Universal LLM Gateway (OpenRouter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Ollama) | RPA record/replay, webhooks, schedules, pipelines | SaaS layer: JWT auth, billing/quota guards, feature flags, audit logging, PII controls, rate limiting
projects.what: A production-minded AI agent platform that turns natural-language automation descriptions into deployable agents, with 4-tier memory, self-learning loops, RPA and multi-agent swarms. 100+ API modules and 40+ core engines behind a FastAPI /api/v1 layer and a Next.js 16 dashboard: create a user, describe an agent in plain language, queue executions, watch memory and learning evolve.
projects.how: FastAPI + async SQLAlchemy backend with REST and WebSocket APIs; Next.js 16 App Router dashboard; PostgreSQL and Redis for state; Prometheus/Grafana observability; hardened middleware (security headers, body limits, rate limits, request IDs); AWS infrastructure written in Terraform (ECS Fargate, RDS, ElastiCache, ALB, CloudFront, WAF, KMS); CI with mocked-LLM tests so the suite runs without provider keys.
projects.outcome: A working, tested, deployable SaaS foundation: full local stack in one docker compose up, CI green, security and compliance docs, and a documented AWS deploy path.

projects.name: Glyph — Intelligent Codebase Scanner & Chat
projects.core_idea: Ask any codebase a question and get an answer grounded in the real code, with clickable file:line citations.
projects.problem: Dropping into an unfamiliar repo costs hours of reading before you can ask a useful question; Glyph indexes the repo and answers only from the actual code, so you verify instead of trust.
projects.features: GitHub or local-folder ingest with live progress | AST chunking via tree-sitter (Python/JS/TS/TSX) so citations land on exact line ranges | two-stage retrieval: hybrid semantic + BM25 recall fused with RRF, then a cross-encoder reranker | grounded streaming answers that refuse when relevance is too weak | live dependency graph, most-depended-on files, command palette | Fast mode with Model2Vec static embeddings (about 100x faster ingest)
projects.what: Ask any codebase a question and get an answer grounded in the real code, with clickable file:line citations. 19 REST endpoints covering ingest, ask, graph, metrics and file viewing, with per-query observability (latency split, tokens, cache hits).
projects.how: FastAPI backend (ingest, chunk, embed, store, retrieve, rerank, answer) and a React/Vite frontend over REST + Server-Sent Events; Chroma vector store keyed per embedding backend; a weekly eval harness in CI clones 5 pinned repos and measures real retrieval hit-rate; continuous deployment pushes images to GHCR and rolls the AWS EC2 stack behind Caddy HTTPS.
projects.outcome: LIVE demo online; 487 tests passing at 100% backend AND frontend coverage; measured 82% top-5 retrieval hit-rate across 5 real repos; the reranker lifts top-1 accuracy from 80% to 90%; 6 CI workflows (lint/types, security, CodeQL, Docker, infra, eval) plus automatic deploy on main.

projects.name: WARZONE: Last Stand — Neon Browser FPS
projects.core_idea: A neon 80s-Miami wave-survival first-person shooter that runs entirely in the browser: no backend, installable as a PWA, works offline after first load.
projects.problem: Shows real-time 3D graphics, game-loop and state-machine engineering in pure JavaScript: a complete game with menus, an economy and combat that anyone can play from a link.
projects.features: 4 operatives with real stat trade-offs | 7 weapons in distinct primary/secondary loadouts | escalating waves with a boss every 5th wave | 3 difficulty tiers | meta-progression: cash banked across runs, Black Market weapon tiers and perks | combat juice: screen shake, hitstop, slow-mo, kill-streak escalation | 13-screen menu flow driven by a small state-machine router | local leaderboard and achievements
projects.what: A neon 80s-Miami wave-survival first-person shooter that runs entirely in the browser: no backend, installable as a PWA, works offline after first load. Boot into a menu hub, pick an operative and loadout, survive waves, bank cash, upgrade at the Black Market, run again stronger; all progress persists in localStorage.
projects.how: Three.js r160 scene with EffectComposer + UnrealBloom post-processing; every game rule (weapons, wave scaling, economy, settings) isolated in a pure dependency-free logic module shared by game and menus so displayed data and in-run behaviour can never drift; Vite 6 build deployed to GitHub Pages; hand-rolled PWA.
projects.outcome: Fully playable in any modern browser and installable offline; 111 Vitest tests cover the entire pure game-logic module; CI, CodeQL and security scans green.

projects.name: ClarityAI — Explainable AI-Text Detection
projects.core_idea: An AI-text detection platform that explains every verdict signal-by-signal: 14 parallel detection signals combined by a stacked ensemble, with a per-sentence heatmap showing where the AI-flavoured passages are.
projects.problem: Single-number AI detectors are black boxes; ClarityAI shows exactly which signals fired and why, and adds plagiarism checking, a humanizer and writing analytics so writers and reviewers can act on the result instead of guessing.
projects.features: 14 parallel deep-detection signals (perplexity/burstiness, GLTR, Fast-DetectGPT, Binoculars, Ghostbuster, zero-shot ensemble, entropy, stylometry, POS patterns, vocabulary richness, repetition, coherence, statistical watermarks, model fingerprints) | stacked meta-learner with a watermark hard-override | per-sentence heatmap + model-family attribution | plagiarism: exact n-grams + semantic embeddings + live source discovery across 6 engines | humanizer rewrite scored before vs after | analytics: readability, tone, grammar, SEO, citations | realtime as-you-type detection over WebSocket | batch processing, history, dashboard, PDF/JSON/CSV export
projects.what: An AI-text detection platform that explains every verdict signal-by-signal: 14 parallel detection signals combined by a stacked ensemble, with a per-sentence heatmap showing where the AI-flavoured passages are. About 50 REST endpoints across 9 routers plus a realtime websocket; all 8 UI pages pass axe accessibility checks; every model download is pinned to an exact Hugging Face revision.
projects.how: React 18 + MUI SPA served by nginx proxying a FastAPI backend that owns the ML pipeline, SQLite persistence and the websocket; detectors fail soft to a flagged neutral result and an empty roster is a loud 503; GLTR calibration was measured on a labelled probe set and pinned as unit tests; 5 CI workflows (CI, Security, CodeQL, Deploy, Dependabot).
projects.outcome: 851 tests passing (741 backend + 110 frontend including accessibility), 77% backend coverage gated in CI; runs 100% free locally on open-weight models; AWS/Terraform deployment written and validated (live demo pending).

projects.name: Orion OS — AI-First Atomic Linux Desktop
projects.core_idea: An AI-first, image-based Linux desktop built on Fedora Atomic with KDE Plasma 6: local-first AI designed into every shell surface, zero telemetry, and atomic updates that can never brick the machine.
projects.problem: Desktop AI today means cloud lock-in and data harvesting; Orion bakes a local-first AI runtime into the launcher, clipboard, terminal, file search and voice, with cloud strictly opt-in per feature and hard spend caps.
projects.features: Declarative BlueBuild recipe builds a signed OCI image and an installable ISO | atomic updates with rollback | supply chain: cosign signatures + syft SBOM + Trivy and Lynis scans in CI | security baseline: SELinux enforcing, firewalld strict, hardened sysctls, DNS-over-HTTPS, restrictive Flatpak, LUKS2+TPM2 full-disk encryption with mandatory passphrase fallback | 12 scoped AI hero features (Copilot, NL launcher, semantic file search, personal RAG, voice control, translate overlay) | every privacy/perf/security promise enforced as a CI test
projects.what: An AI-first, image-based Linux desktop built on Fedora Atomic with KDE Plasma 6: local-first AI designed into every shell surface, zero telemetry, and atomic updates that can never brick the machine. Builds a complete, installable, security-hardened Linux distribution from a declarative recipe, with CI producing the signed image and the Calamares ISO.
projects.how: A BlueBuild recipe layers Orion modules onto the aurora-dx:43 base image; GitHub Actions runs lint, image build, ISO build, Trivy + Lynis security scans, CodeQL and VM smoke tests; images are published to GHCR and cosign-signed.
projects.outcome: Working pre-alpha: signed image and ISO build pipelines green across 6+ CI workflows; frozen ADR-governed stack and full architecture documentation.

projects.name: Kestrel — Multi-Source Job Discovery Engine
projects.core_idea: A pure, typed TypeScript engine that expands one IT domain into 835+ real-world title aliases, sweeps 8 sources across about 220 public ATS boards, verifies every link is live, scores apply-readiness and ranks the best matches.
projects.problem: Hunting early-career IT roles means manually checking dozens of noisy boards full of stale or too-senior posts; Kestrel automates the whole sweep and only surfaces verified, genuinely new postings.
projects.features: 20 locked IT domains expanded into 835+ title aliases | 8 sources / ~220 boards: Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, RemoteOK keyless plus Adzuna, Jooble, SerpAPI, ScrapeGraphAI key-gated | Zod-validated ingestion; malformed rows quarantined and reported, never silently dropped | seniority filter with word-boundary guards | HEAD-then-GET live-link verification with retry/backoff | deterministic, explainable ranker with per-job score breakdown (no LLM, reproducible and free) | visa/Stamp 1G/sponsorship flags, salary parsing, work-mode, location normalisation, freshness | cross-run dedup via a persistent seen-store | Telegram digest + React/MUI dashboard
projects.what: A pure, typed TypeScript engine that expands one IT domain into 835+ real-world title aliases, sweeps 8 sources across about 220 public ATS boards, verifies every link is live, scores apply-readiness and ranks the best matches. The engine is a pure typed library; the CLI, web dashboard and n8n workflow are thin adapters with injected HTTP transport, so every rule is unit-tested in isolation and the same code drives every surface.
projects.how: A staged pipeline of pure, separately tested functions (resolve domains, plan requests, run sources concurrently, parse, validate, dedupe, filter, match, verify links, enrich, rank, annotate, deliver) with bounded concurrency, exponential backoff and per-source failure isolation so one dead source never stops a scan.
projects.outcome: 624 tests (about 97% line coverage) parametrised across all 20 domains and 8 source shapes; production dashboard scores Lighthouse 94 performance / 98 accessibility / 96 best-practices; a recent live run processed 2,450 candidates into 75 matches and 12 ranked verified results.

projects.name: Litmus — ATS + AI-Detection Resume Scanner
projects.core_idea: The litmus test a resume takes before any human reads it: ATS compatibility and AI-detection risk scored in one pass, with a prioritized fix for everything it finds.
projects.problem: Resumes are filtered twice before a human sees them, once by ATS keyword matching and increasingly by AI-detection tooling; Litmus is a scanner that tests both axes at once and tells you exactly what to fix.
projects.features: Dual-axis scan in under 3 seconds | 5-dimension ATS breakdown | 19 explainable AI signals with a per-bullet risk heatmap | fix generator: every finding becomes a concrete suggestion with an example rewrite | humanizer with layered transforms (rule-based + optional free ML paraphrase) | PDF/DOCX upload, bulk scanning, version comparison, PDF report export | grammar and Flesch-Kincaid readability checks | per-IP rate limiting; private by design, nothing stored server-side
projects.what: The litmus test a resume takes before any human reads it: ATS compatibility and AI-detection risk scored in one pass, with a prioritized fix for everything it finds. 9 REST endpoints (full scan, file, bulk, quick, compare, humanize, PDF export, keyword extraction, health); scan history lives only in the browser's localStorage; the backend is fully stateless.
projects.how: Independent engine modules (ATS, 19-signal AI detection, humanizer, grammar, readability, fix generator, scoring, parsers) with a degraded_mode contract so one failing engine degrades the scan instead of failing it; the ML classifier is one vote of 19, never a dependency, with full offline fallback; the test suite blocks all external HTTP by construction.
projects.outcome: 145 tests (116 backend + 29 frontend), 79% backend coverage; quick scans return in about 130 ms; CI with gitleaks, Trivy and CodeQL reports 0 known CVEs; Docker, Render and Vercel deploy manifests included.

projects.name: SkyMetrics — Airline Customer Intelligence
projects.core_idea: An airline customer-intelligence platform for British Airways: review sentiment, aspect analysis, topic mining, booking-completion prediction, live flight tracking and a RAG chatbot in one tested product.
projects.problem: Airlines sit on a flood of public customer feedback but rarely turn it into decisions; SkyMetrics scores the reviews, predicts booking completion and lets you question the data in natural language.
projects.features: TextBlob baseline plus optional DistilBERT transformer sentiment | aspect-based scoring across 7 service aspects (seat, food, staff, delay, baggage, value, wifi) | TF-IDF topic mining | Random Forest booking-completion prediction served over HTTP | XGBoost + SHAP feature-attribution analysis | live airborne BA flights from the OpenSky Network plotted on a map | IAG share-price enrichment | LLM review summariser and a RAG chatbot answering with cited review sources
projects.what: An airline customer-intelligence platform for British Airways: review sentiment, aspect analysis, topic mining, booking-completion prediction, live flight tracking and a RAG chatbot in one tested product. 7 API endpoints (sentiment, aspects, live flights, predict, summary, chat, health) plus a Streamlit dashboard; began as the British Airways Forage data-science brief and was expanded into a fully tested, containerised product.
projects.how: Scrapers with a fetch/parse split (parsers unit-tested, network mocked) load Skytrax reviews, OpenSky flights and share prices into SQLite; the NLP, ML and LLM layers serve through FastAPI and the Streamlit dashboard consumes the API; TF-IDF retrieval keeps the RAG chatbot deterministic and free; a slim Docker image excludes heavy training dependencies.
projects.outcome: 81 unit tests with all network and LLM calls mocked; full CI with ruff, mypy, bandit, pip-audit, gitleaks, Trivy and CodeQL; one-command docker compose up runs API and dashboard together.

projects.name: PolyCortex — ML Prediction-Market Trading System
projects.core_idea: A neural trading system for Polymarket prediction markets: Bayesian edge detection plus a TCN neural ensemble, isotonic probability calibration, HMM regime detection and fractional-Kelly sizing with defense-in-depth risk controls.
projects.problem: Extracting a tradeable edge from prediction-market prices requires calibrated probabilities, regime awareness and strict risk management; PolyCortex wires all of it into one unattended, fail-safe pipeline.
projects.features: Bayesian edge + TCN ensemble, regime-weighted by a 3-state HMM | isotonic probability calibration | features: logit returns, RSI, volume momentum, order-book imbalance, time decay, cross-market | position sizing: fractional Kelly scaled by confidence, volatility and regime, with per-position/portfolio/category caps | 3-tier drawdown circuit breakers: halt new trades at 15%, liquidate at 20% | execution: limit orders, order splitting, TP/SL brackets, GTT, paper mode with partial-fill simulation | full backtester with fees, slippage and spread-impact realism | SQLite P&L, Brier calibration tracking, online signal-weight learner | kill switch, heartbeat and health checks
projects.what: A neural trading system for Polymarket prediction markets: Bayesian edge detection plus a TCN neural ensemble, isotonic probability calibration, HMM regime detection and fractional-Kelly sizing with defense-in-depth risk controls. Scans Gamma API markets, reads the CLOB order book, folds in Claude news sentiment (cached), sizes positions and executes through py-clob-client, with a Streamlit dashboard and a JSONL alert stream.
projects.how: Event-driven Python orchestrator with an order state machine, WebSocket client, TWAP and trailing stops, batch orders, anomaly detector, graceful shutdown and retry/circuit breakers; Dockerised with a HEALTHCHECK; paper-trading engine simulates partial fills and slippage before any real USDC.
projects.outcome: 249 tests passing; CI, Security, CodeQL and Docs workflows green; runs unattended in Docker with documented emergency kill-switch procedures.

projects.name: Meridian — Real-Time Global Intelligence Dashboard
projects.core_idea: A real-time global intelligence dashboard that aggregates 11+ unreliable public APIs into one validated, cached, failure-isolated interface, live on Vercel.
projects.problem: Public data is scattered across inconsistent APIs with rate limits and flaky uptime; Meridian normalises everything through server-side routes with runtime validation and circuit breakers before the browser ever sees it.
projects.features: Live world counters (population, emissions, energy, internet activity, economy) | weather, earthquakes, markets, forex, space/ISS, air quality, news and technology tabs | 3D WebGL globe hero | circuit breaker per provider + endpoint-specific cache and revalidation windows | Zod validation of every external response with shared inferred TypeScript types | error boundaries isolate individual tab failures | command palette and keyboard navigation | system-health tab and /api/health-check endpoint used as the deploy smoke test
projects.what: A real-time global intelligence dashboard that aggregates 11+ unreliable public APIs into one validated, cached, failure-isolated interface, live on Vercel. Aggregates Open-Meteo, USGS, CoinGecko, Frankfurter, World Bank, REST Countries, NASA, OpenAQ, GitHub, Hacker News and NewsAPI; runs free by default, optional keys unlock richer NASA/news/globe data.
projects.how: Every external call goes through Next.js API routes (never the browser) wrapped in a circuit breaker with per-endpoint caching; SWR manages stale-while-revalidate polling per data category; CI runs lint, typecheck, tests and a production build; Dockerfile supports containerised deployment.
projects.outcome: Deployed and LIVE at meridian.vercel.app with CI green; the health-check endpoint doubles as the production smoke test after each deploy.

projects.name: QuantumLedger — AI Stock & Crypto Portfolio Tracker
projects.core_idea: A real-time stock and crypto portfolio tracker with AI-assisted market intelligence: a web SPA plus a React Native mobile client on one FastAPI backend.
projects.problem: Investors juggle separate tools for holdings, market data and analysis; QuantumLedger unifies portfolio tracking, live markets, analytics/backtesting and AI insights behind one authenticated API.
projects.features: Portfolio: holdings, transactions, P/L, allocation donut, goals and DCA | live markets: stock + crypto search, watchlists, screeners, top gainers/losers | analytics: metrics, risk analysis, backtesting, ML-assisted prediction | AI insights: chat assistant, sentiment radar, smart-money and whale signals | production-shaped: JWT/httpOnly-cookie auth, rate limiting, health checks, Swagger docs | guest mode with a pre-loaded sample portfolio
projects.what: A real-time stock and crypto portfolio tracker with AI-assisted market intelligence: a web SPA plus a React Native mobile client on one FastAPI backend. About 38 routers and 21 services on the backend serving both the web SPA and the React Native mobile client with real market data from five providers.
projects.how: FastAPI + SQLAlchemy 2 + Pydantic backend; React 18 + Vite + Tailwind SPA and a React Native mobile client; market data from yfinance, CoinGecko, NewsAPI, Alpha Vantage and FRED; infrastructure written as Terraform on AWS with Docker and Vercel manifests and GitHub Actions CI.
projects.outcome: A working, tested, deployable full-stack fintech application with web and mobile interfaces: 32 backend tests plus a frontend Vitest suite, self-contained test setup, CI + Security + CodeQL green.
